svg.text: Azure Virtual WAN Without Bow-Tie: C1 vs. Region A Failure
Failure Outcome A: C1 Peering Outage (Region A Workloads Still Up)
- Connected MPLS: Region A SURVIVES without Bow-Tie! Branch 1 -> MPLS -> C2 -> vHUB 2 -> 1.
- MPLS Cost: Branch 1 traffic traverses customer MPLS WAN + vWAN inter-hub backbone.
- Isolated Branch 1 (No MPLS): Loses Azure access because C1 (and Global Reach on C1) is down.
- Inter-Region East-West: Region A <-> Region B continues natively over vWAN mesh.
B. Full Azure Region A Outage
Failure Outcome B: Full Azure Region A Outage (Peering C1 Healthy)
- Orphaned Circuit: Losing Region A takes down vHUB 1, orphaning C1 from vWAN!
- MPLS Saturation: Branch 1 hauls 100% of DR traffic via MPLS -> Branch 2 -> C2 -> vHUB 2.
- Isolated Branch 1 (No MPLS): CUT OFF from Region B DR unless Global Reach (C1<->C2) is ON!
- Global Reach Rescue: Global Reach C1 <-> C2 lets C1 transit MSEE backbone to C2 -> vHUB 2.
Azure Networking Field Architect Handbook | Part 3: Hybrid Connectivity
